title: Degree of the pairing
statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell}\}$ and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be perfect over $\Lambda_X$. The shift convention $H^r(C[m])=H^{r+m}(C)$ identifies the degree-zero part of the derived pairing $\beta _K$ of [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing] with the pairings

$$
\langle -,-\rangle _i:\   H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr) \longrightarrow \Lambda \qquad (i\in \mathbf Z).
$$

Before inserting the Tate twist, the same morphism is the line-valued pairing

$$
H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee ) \longrightarrow \Lambda(-d),
$$

obtained by eliminating the invertible twist $\Lambda _X(d)$ of the second factor through the canonical isomorphism $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee (d))\cong H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\otimes _\Lambda \Lambda (d)$ and using the twist inverse.

proof.text: *Degree zero.* By [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing], $\beta_K$ is the composite of the mixed-support cup product $\smile_c$, of $R\Gamma_c(\operatorname{ev}_K(d))[2d]$ and of the normalized smooth trace $\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,\Lambda}:R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X(d))[2d]\to\Lambda$; each is a morphism of the derived category, so $\beta_K$ is a morphism $R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]\to\Lambda$ of degree zero (the top cohomology of the shifted source of the trace sits in degree $2d-2d=0$). Write $C=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ and $D=R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))$. For all integers $i,j$ there is the canonical map $H^i(C)\otimes_\Lambda H^j(D[2d])\to H^{i+j}(C\otimes^L_\Lambda D[2d])$, sending the classes of cocycles $x,y$ of a K-flat representative to the class of $x\otimes y$. Taking $j=-i$ and composing with $H^0(\beta_K)$ gives a $\Lambda$-bilinear pairing $H^i(C)\times H^{-i}(D[2d])\to H^0(\Lambda)=\Lambda$; these, for $i\in\mathbf Z$, are the components of the degree-zero part of $\beta_K$. By the shift convention $H^r(C'[m])=H^{r+m}(C')$, $H^{-i}(D[2d])=H^{2d-i}(D)=H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))$, which gives $\langle-,-\rangle_i:H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))\to\Lambda$. (For $i=0$ the second factor is $H^{2d}(X,K^\vee(d))$; for $i$ outside the bounded range of $C$ or of $D[2d]$ both the groups and the pairing are zero.)

proof.text: *The twist line on $X$ is constant.* Here $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ with $k$ algebraically closed and $\ell\neq p$. For $r\geq1$ the group $\mu_{\ell^r}(k)$ is cyclic of order $\ell^r$, and the map $(\mu_{\ell^r}(k))_X\to\mu_{\ell^r,X}$ sending a constant to the corresponding constant function is an isomorphism of sheaves on the pro-etale site of $X$, with $\mu_{\ell^r,X}$ as in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]: if $U\to X$ is an object and $u\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U^\times)$ satisfies $u^{\ell^r}=1$, the elements $u-\zeta$ ($\zeta\in\mu_{\ell^r}(k)$) generate pairwise comaximal ideals, since $(u-\zeta)-(u-\zeta')=\zeta'-\zeta$ is a unit ($\ell$ invertible in $k$), and their product is $u^{\ell^r}-1=0$; by the Chinese remainder theorem $U$ is the disjoint union of the open and closed subschemes $U_\zeta=V(u-\zeta)$, on which $u=\zeta$, so $u$ is a locally constant $\mu_{\ell^r}(k)$-valued function, and conversely; injectivity is clear. These isomorphisms are compatible with the transition maps $u\mapsto u^\ell$, which are surjective on $\mu_{\ell^{r+1}}(k)\to\mu_{\ell^r}(k)$. Hence $T=\varprojlim_r\mu_{\ell^r}(k)$ is a free $\mathbf Z_\ell$-module of rank one, and a compatible system of generators $\zeta=(\zeta_r)_r$ gives $\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,X}=\varprojlim_r(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_r\mu_{\ell^r,X}=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_X$, $1\mapsto\zeta$; the resulting isomorphism $\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,X}\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}T\cong\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_X$ does not depend on $\zeta$. With $\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,X}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_X}(\mathcal O_E)_X\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ (clause 3 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]) this gives $\mathcal O_E(1)_X\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_E(1)$ with $\mathcal O_E(1)=T\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}\mathcal O_E$, free of rank one over $\mathcal O_E$. Put $\Lambda(1)=\mathcal O_E(1)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\Lambda$ (for $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ through a finite stage $E$), $\Lambda(m)=\Lambda(1)^{\otimes_\Lambda m}$ for $m\geq0$ and $\Lambda(m)=\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(\Lambda(-m),\Lambda)$ for $m<0$: free $\Lambda$-modules of rank one. Since tensor powers, sheaf Hom into $\Lambda_X$, reduction to $A_{E,n}$ and scalar extension of $\Lambda_X\otimes_\Lambda M$ with $M$ free of rank one are computed on $M$, the formulas of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] give $\Lambda(m)_X\cong\Lambda_X\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda(m)$ for every $m\in\mathbf Z$ (for $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ on the integral representative), compatibly with the evaluations $\Lambda(m)_X\otimes\Lambda(-m)_X\to\Lambda_X$ and $\Lambda(m)\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda(-m)\to\Lambda$, which are isomorphisms. In particular $\Lambda(-d)=\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(\Lambda(d),\Lambda)$. (For $X=s$ this line is the twist line $H^0(s,\Lambda(m)_s)$ of the point.)

proof.text: *Elimination of the twist.* By the previous step and the definition $K(m)=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\Lambda(m)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], $K^\vee(d)\cong K^\vee\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}(\Lambda_X\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda(d))\cong K^\vee\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda(d)$, the termwise tensor product with the free rank-one module $\Lambda(d)$. The canonical $\Lambda$-linear map $R\Gamma(X,K^\vee)\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda(d)\to R\Gamma(X,K^\vee\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda(d))$, $c\otimes\lambda\mapsto c\otimes\lambda$ on a K-injective representative, is an isomorphism: after the choice of a basis $e$ of $\Lambda(d)$ both sides are $R\Gamma(X,K^\vee)$ and the map is the identity, and the map itself does not involve $e$. Taking $H^{2d-i}$ gives the canonical isomorphism $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))\cong H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda(d)$. Through it, $\langle-,-\rangle_i$ of the first step becomes a $\Lambda$-linear map $H_c^i(X,K)\otimes_\Lambda H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda(d)\to\Lambda$, and by the tensor–Hom adjunction for $\Lambda$-modules a $\Lambda$-linear map $H_c^i(X,K)\otimes_\Lambda H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)\to\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(\Lambda(d),\Lambda)=\Lambda(-d)$, the last identification being the twist inverse of the previous step. This is the line-valued pairing $H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)\to\Lambda(-d)$; it is the same morphism, as it is obtained from $\langle-,-\rangle_i$ only by the canonical isomorphisms above and is recovered from it by evaluating on $\Lambda(d)$.

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell}\}$ and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be perfect over $\Lambda_X$. The shift convention $H^r(C[m])=H^{r+m}(C)$ identifies the degree-zero part of the derived pairing $\beta _K$ of [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing] with the pairings

$$
\langle -,-\rangle _i:\   H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr) \longrightarrow \Lambda \qquad (i\in \mathbf Z).
$$

Before inserting the Tate twist, the same morphism is the line-valued pairing

obtained by eliminating the invertible twist $\Lambda _X(d)$ of the second factor through the canonical isomorphism $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee (d))\cong H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\otimes _\Lambda \Lambda (d)$ and using the twist inverse.

proof.text: The degree of $\beta _K$ is zero: both the mixed-support cup product and the evaluation are degree-preserving, and the trace $\operatorname {Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,\Lambda }$ has degree zero on the shifted complex $R\Gamma _c(X,\Lambda _X(d))[2d]$, whose top cohomology sits in degree $2d-2d=0$. Unpacking $H^r(C[m])=H^{r+m}(C)$ in the second variable gives $H^0\bigl(R\Gamma (X,K^\vee (d))[2d]\bigr)=H^{2d}(X,K^\vee (d))$ and, more generally, decomposing into cohomological degrees, the degree-zero part of the pairing pairs $H_c^i(X,K)$ against $H^{-i}\bigl(R\Gamma (X,K^\vee (d))[2d]\bigr)=H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee (d))$. For the line-valued form, the twist $\Lambda _X(d)=\Lambda _X\otimes _\Lambda \Lambda (d)$ with $\Lambda (d)$ the invertible locally constant rank-one twist sheaf of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] is eliminated by tensoring the pairing with its twist inverse $\Lambda(-d)$ and using the canonical isomorphisms $\Lambda (d)\otimes _\Lambda \Lambda (-d)\cong \Lambda$: this is the identification of $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee (d))$ with $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\otimes _\Lambda \Lambda (d)$ (by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], the twist of a complex commutes with the global sections), so the pairing becomes $H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\to \Lambda(-d)$.

Repaired in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-poincare-duality/prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing.json (only proof, proof_deps and split_report changed) by splitting the step into three. (1) Degree zero: the explicit Kunneth map and the shift H^{-i}(D[2d])=H^{2d-i}. (2) Over algebraically closed k, mu_{l^r,X} is the constant sheaf (Chinese remainder argument, l invertible), so Z_l(1)_X = Z_l-hat tensor T_l(k), and Lambda(m)_X = Lambda_X tensor Lambda(m) with Lambda(m) free of rank one. This uses clause 3 of lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free, which is on the unit route (sk-def-sf-admissible) and makes no cycle. (3) RGamma(X,K(d)) = RGamma(X,K) tensor Lambda(d), then tensor-Hom adjunction into Lambda(-d)=Hom(Lambda(d),Lambda).
